title: A walk shows only the pictures it took this time
goal: When a scripted run of the app is re-run, the pictures it took last time are still sitting in its output folder. A run that stopped early leaves a folder full of pictures from a healthier run, and whoever reads it, agent or person, cannot tell which run any of them came from. The pictures in a run folder should be that run's pictures and nothing else.
notes:
REPRODUCED 2026-09-18 02:49 while building the crash reporting in a-walk-whose-app-died-says-the-app-died.

The probe was built with the layer-rename fix reverted (git checkout 6bfe4969^ -- Sources/Photonz/EditorState.swift Sources/PhotonzCore/History.swift), so unique-layer-names-walk aborts at step 17 (renameSelectedLayer). Its last log line is step 16:

  [16 wait] 0.5s asked, quiet after 0.10s

and the run photographed exactly one thing, step 13:

  [0 capture] names-1-four-shapes-sc.png 2800x2056

yet the folder it printed at the end held six pictures:

  ==> Output: /tmp/photonz-playtest/unique-layer-names
  log.json
  names-1-four-shapes-sc.png
  names-1-four-shapes.png
  names-2-after-rename-sc.png
  names-2-after-rename.png
  names-3-after-paste-sc.png
  names-3-after-paste.png

names-2 and names-3 are from an earlier passing run: those steps never ran. Scripts/playtest.sh only does `rm -f "$OUT/done.json"` before launching (line 51), so everything else from the last run survives.

Why it matters beyond tidiness: an audit is required to ship a real -sc.png from a walk, and the runner writing that audit picks the file out of this folder. A crashed or cut-short run hands it a picture of an app that was working, taken minutes or days earlier, with nothing to say so. Clearing the folder (or writing each run into its own subfolder) is the fix; if renders are cleared, keep in mind a walk that fails at step 2 should still leave the one picture it took.
acceptance: A walk that stops part way leaves no picture from any earlier run in its output folder
A walk that completes leaves exactly the pictures it took, and its log and its done.json
Re-running the same walk twice in a row leaves the same set of files both times

log.note: Triage 2026-09-18: moved from the back of p2 to third. A run folder that still holds an earlier run's pictures makes every audit photograph ambiguous, and an audit is the user's only window into what shipped, so this ranks above the features behind it.

Reproduced on the pre-fix probe: planted 9-from-an-older-run-sc.png in /tmp/photonz-playtest/toolbar-row-narrow, re-ran toolbar-row-narrow-walk --no-build, and the planted picture was still in the folder's listing at the end.

Fix: a run empties its output folder before it writes anything (PlaytestHarness.prepareOutput). How much of the folder it may claim is PlaytestOutputFolder in PhotonzCore, unit tested (10 tests): its own folder under /tmp/photonz-playtest goes whole minus hidden files; a folder anywhere else is assumed shared (a walk could point out at the folder holding the other 530 walk scripts) so only log.json, done.json and the three menu-shot notes go, and the run says in its log that other pictures there may be old. The clearing is said in the log's first line.

Verified all three acceptance items: a walk stopping at step 4 left only 1-took-this-one{,-sc}.png plus log/done and neither planted picture; a completed toolbar-row-narrow-walk left exactly its two pictures, their offscreen twins, two panel readings, log.json and done.json; two runs back to back listed identical file sets. Scripts/test.sh: 8352 tests in 669 suites, all passing. Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build narrow: 6 passed, 0 failed, 2 could not run (screen locked, pre-existing).

left rough: a walk refused because the screen is locked clears its folder before it discovers it cannot run, so a Mac that stays locked gradually empties the folders of every name-dependent walk. Deliberate (a refusal took no pictures, so leaving an older run's under a fresh done.json is the confusion this fixes) and in the audit's rough list; not filed.

A run empties its output folder before it writes anything, so a folder holds only that run's pictures. Rule in PlaytestOutputFolder (PhotonzCore, 10 unit tests), applied in PlaytestHarness.prepareOutput and said in the log's first line; Scripts/playtest.sh also clears a stale log.json for the case where the app dies before the harness starts. Reproduced on the pre-fix probe, then verified: a walk failing at step 4 left only the picture it reached, a completed walk left exactly its own files, two runs in a row left identical sets. Scripts/test.sh green (8352 tests); playtest-all --no-build narrow 6 passed / 0 failed / 2 refused by the lock. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-19-a-walk-shows-only-its-own-pictures.json. Full sweep requested. Commit c16eba7f.
